page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the c3 server family. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz, featuring 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities paired with weaker multi-core scaling. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average category, supported by average performance in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, are classified as weak. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block and write large block speeds registering in the weak tier at 28.42 GB/sec and 21.13 GB/sec respectively.

Despite the lower multi-core performance, the underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning and matrix operations. This is reflected in average text processing and static web serving throughput of 6.68 GB/sec. The instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, single-threaded applications, and lightweight text processing tasks where massive multi-core scaling or high memory bandwidth is not a primary requirement.
